syllabus_topics: Intuitive theory of sets, relations, and functions
Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) and its efficient computation (FFT)
Analysis of imperative program efficiency in the worst and average cases
Determination of closed forms for summations of elementary terms
Hoare logic for partial and total correctness of imperative programs
Total correctness of search and sorting algorithms
assessment_rules: The final grade is the weighted average of the scores obtained in 3 tests (weights: 30%, 35%, 35%). Each test is graded out of 20 points. The score for each test can be improved independently during the resit exam period. Students can recover the grade of one, two, or all three tests, with the best score between the in-class test and the resit test counting for each.
bibliography: Jonathan L. Gross, Combinatorial Methods with Computer Applications, Chapman & Hall CRC, 2008 (main)
Ronald L. Graham, Donald E. Knuth e Oren Patashnik, Concrete Mathematics: A foundation for computer science, Addison-Wesley Publishing Company, 1994 (main)
José Félix Costa e Paula Gouveia, Matemática Discreta, IST Press, 2019 (main)
institution: Universidade De Lisboa — LEIC-A Eng. Informática e de Computadores (IST)
degree: Licenciatura em Engenharia Informática e de Computadores - Alameda (LEIC-A)
